details.summary: An excellent, highly compliant breakfast recipe that creatively uses white beans and frozen broccoli to deliver a high-fiber, high-protein start to the day. It perfectly respects the book's nutritional targets, flavor profile requirements, and 30-minute timeframe.

dimensions.feedback: The savory, smoky flavor profile of the frittata pairs excellently with the bright, sweet acidity of the fresh orange segments served on the side.
All ingredients are perfectly matched between the ingredient list and the step-by-step instructions.
Excellent instruction design. Time ranges, mid-point checks, and clear visual doneness cues (e.g., 'edges begin to set', 'center is fully set') are used throughout.
A skillet frittata with beans and broccoli fits the Modern American breakfast profile seamlessly.
Starting the frittata on the stovetop to cook the vegetables and set the edges, then finishing it in the oven, is the ideal and standard method for this dish.
The macronutrient values are highly plausible and align correctly with the ingredients and quantities provided.
The title and introduction accurately reflect the ingredients and process. The tone is warm and practical, avoiding any banned health claims.
A highly appetizing and visually pleasing recipe. Folding hearty white beans into a frittata is a clever, delicious way to boost morning fiber.

Outstanding alignment with the dual-condition goal. It limits saturated fat by diluting whole eggs with liquid whites and using just a garnish of cheese, while providing superb fiber via beans and broccoli.

Perfect handling of carbohydrates. Zero added sugar, with a robust 51.1g of total carbs coming from extremely high-quality sources (navy beans and whole fresh oranges), fitting the target window flawlessly.
Nails the breakfast chapter intent: 34g of protein and 13g of fiber easily meet the tier's minimums, ensuring a filling meal that prevents mid-morning blood sugar crashes.

Fully realistic within 30 minutes. The prep is minimal thanks to frozen broccoli, and the oven preheats while the stovetop steps take place. All ingredients are easy to find at any mainstream supermarket.
